script: Spread and total were not saved, so this is form-only: Detroit has been the engine (Jahmyr Gibbs 45 carries for 208 yards, Amon-Ra St. Brown 27 targets for 209) while the Jets have ground it out (Breece Hall 38 carries for 131, Garrett Wilson 14 targets for 136). NYJ's defense is the sturdier unit (4.09 YPC, 4 runs of 10+, 1 pass of 20+ on 67 attempts), so the inferred script is Detroit sustaining drives through Gibbs and St. Brown, with New York manufacturing yards on the ground and underneath rather than over the top.
who_goes_off: Breece Hall is the Jet who fits the leak: Detroit has allowed 5.12 YPC and 10 runs of 10+, and Hall already has 79 receiving yards on 7 targets and 2 air yards, the checkdown profile a 43% blitz feeds. Jahmyr Gibbs has the raw volume (208 rush yards, 13 targets, 91 rec yards) but NYJ's 4.09 YPC and 4 explosive runs allowed cap him more than his own form implies.
weak_spot: Detroit's real hole is the middle, not the outside corners: 13.27 YPA on 15 middle attempts versus 4.11 YPA left (27 att) and 7.91 right (44 att), plus a run fit that has already surrendered 10 gains of 10+. That points at backs and short-area targets (Hall's 2 air yards, Kenyon Sadiq's 6 targets) rather than Garrett Wilson's 152 air yards. NYJ has no comparable crack — middle is their softest at 5.91 YPA on only 11 attempts, and the right side is 3.36.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for NYJ@DET, so no fallout is priced for Hall, Gibbs, St. Brown, LaPorta, or the Jets' tight ends.
qb_vs_blitz: Jets QB EPA is flat either way (0.18 on 20 blitz dropbacks, 0.18 with no blitz), so Detroit's 43% blitz rate does not swing the dropback — it just dumps the ball to Hall. Jared Goff is the one with a blitz edge (0.33 EPA on 23 blitz dropbacks vs 0.18 without), but the Jets blitz only 28%, so he is unlikely to see the pressure looks he has crushed.

picks.why: Hall has 79 receiving yards on 7 targets and 2 air yards in these two games, about 39.5 a game, against a 21.5 line. Detroit blitzes 43% and has been gashed in the middle at 13.27 YPA, which is where a 2-air-yard back lives, and the Jets' QB does not lose EPA when blitzed (0.18/0.18), so the dump-offs should keep coming even if Detroit leads.

Jameson Williams has 78 yards on 13 targets despite 177 air yards (6.0 yards per target) against a 54 line, so he already needs a spike. NYJ has allowed 1 pass of 20+ in 67 attempts and holds every side under 6.0 YPA (left 5.73, middle 5.91, right 3.36), the wrong defense for a 13.6 aDOT receiver to clear 54.
